thread:
jorge: Quick sanity check — replay harness vs synthetic looks inconsistent. Streaming p95 spikes on short-turn tests but nonstreaming is fine. anyone seen this?

emily: +1 saw this yesterday. streaming with chunk_size=16 had much worse tail. suspect client read loop + kernel selector. :thinking:

sanjay: Important to make the runs apples-to-apples first: same model binary, same quantization, same batch_size, identical sequence-length distribution. Are we replaying the exact request timing or just request order?

jorge: replay harness replays timings (we use wall-time spacing) and preserves prompt histograms. config used: `--replay --preserve-timing --kv-prewarm=true`

max: sharing quick numbers from last run: non-streaming p95=45ms, streaming p95=140ms, throughput similar. workload = 1k concurrent clients, avg seq=48, median seq=12.

lisa: that pattern screams kernel-launch overhead for tiny chunks. streaming breaks sequences into small chunks which reduces amortization of kernel startup costs. also KV cache warm/cold matters for early tokens.

jorge: possible that kernel selector picks a kernel optimized for long sequences only when chunk >= threshold. if chunk < threshold, we do more launches.

sanjay: I instrumented kernel launches yesterday — streaming path did ~3x kernel launches for short-turn flows. patched profiler output attached (excerpt):
```
# stream_short_turn.prof
kernel_launch_count: 3124
avg_kernel_latency_ms: 0.48
kernel_overhead_ms_total: 1500
```

max: posted the bench command we used:
```
./bench --model redwood-v1 --quant q4_0 --clients 1000 --preserve-timing --stream --chunk_size 16 --batch_limit 64
```

emily: try two controlled experiments to isolate variables: 1) identical input stream but disable server streaming (server emits full response at end). 2) enable streaming but use chunk_size equal to full seq (simulate streaming without chunking). compare kernel_launch_count and write syscall patterns.

infra-bot: quick run results for emily's tests:
```
run A (streaming, chunk=16): p95=138ms, kernel_launches=3200, nvlink_util=72%
run B (nonstreaming): p95=46ms, kernel_launches=1100, nvlink_util=75%
run C (streaming, chunk=full_seq): p95=50ms, kernel_launches=1150
```

lisa: so when streaming with full_seq chunking behaves like non-streaming. points to chunking+kernel selection overhead.

jorge: also saw client backpressure effects. if client read loop uses a coarse poll interval, server TCP send buffers fill and write() blocks, which prevents the runtime from processing other ready requests and causes smaller effective batches.

max: example bad client loop: `while (!done) { sleep(10ms); read(fd); }` good one: `while (!done) { read(fd, buf, 8k); }` — continuous draining avoids head-of-line blocking on the socket.

sanjay: on the runtime side we also saw that when write() blocks we end up flushing partial KV caches more often, increasing memory copies and stalling the exec thread. KV hit ratio dropped ~6% during blocked periods.

jorge: concrete regression: I bisected to commit abc1234 that relaxed the kernel selector threshold from 64->32 tokens to try to save memory for long sequences. That made more tiny-launch kernels for short chunks.

emily: commit abc1234 also changed batching heuristic to prefer lower latency by favouring smaller batches when queue depth fluctuates. combined effect = worse tail for streaming.

lisa: mitigation options: 1) revert threshold change OR make threshold adaptive to chunk_size; 2) tune batching heuristic to prefer batching across short-chunk streams when latency SLO allows; 3) improve client SDK read loop docs and default to continuous reads.

max: quick patch idea: if streaming && chunk_size < 32 then force kernel_choice="large_seq" and enable micro-batching in runtime so a single kernel handles multiple chunks from different requests. rough perf win estimate: -30% p95.

ci-bench-bot: queued a controlled run with adaptive selector patch (branch: runtime/adaptive-kernel) against the same workload. results will be posted in ~20m.

jorge: checklist for replicable apples-to-apples experiments (putting here so we don't forget):
- identical model binary + quantization flag
- same seed for RNG in replay harness
- preserve timing vs order must be explicit
- same sequence-length histogram (or force sample to match)
- KV cache prewarm policy documented and consistent
- client SDK read loop behavior controlled (drain vs poll)
- measure kernel_launch_count, nvlink, gpu_util, cpu steal, syscall backpressure (blocked write counts)
- collect perf traces (NVIDIA Nsight / CUPTI) and runtime profiler output

emily: also worth adding a small microbenchmark that measures kernel launch cost vs token processing cost for each kernel variant so kernel selector can make cost-based decisions.

sanjay: agreed. i'll add kernel-launch microbench and a short test that runs streaming with synthetic chunk sizes [4,8,16,32,64,full] and reports per-chunk kernel launches.

jorge: great. follow-ups: sanjay + max to run microbench and adaptive-kernel branch. emily to add client read-loop guidance in SDK repo. lisa to open a perf regression ticket for abc1234 with the bisect notes. i'll wait on ci-bench-bot results then we can decide revert vs adaptive. :+1:

ci-bench-bot: adaptive-kernel run complete: streaming p95=98ms (-30% vs baseline streaming), non-streaming unchanged. kernel_launch_count reduced by 48%. full logs: link://ci/1729

jorge: terrific. leaving action items in the ticket. thanks all. :rocket:
